primary_meaning: the Holy Spirit (as empowering presence, anointing, and fuel for spiritual light/witness)

alternatives.meaning: spiritual preparedness, readiness, or vigilance for Christ's return
faith, grace, or an enduring personal relationship with God
good works, righteous deeds, or practical charity that sustains witness
joy, gladness, or healing/consolation (broader oil symbolism occasionally applied)

notes: Across historic and modern Christian interpretation, oil (including lamp oil) is most consistently linked to the Holy Spirit; the Parable of the Ten Virgins supplies the main lamp-oil context and generates secondary readings of readiness/faith/works, yet these are typically understood as effects or evidences of the Spirit rather than replacements for that primary symbolism. No major tradition rejects the Spirit association for oil in general.
